Description: The sphenoidal sinuses are located in the body of the sphenoid bone and may extend into its wings. They are unevenly divided and separated by a bony septum. Only thin plates of bone separate the sinuses from several important structures: the optic nerves and optic chiasm, pituitary gland, internal carotid arteries and cavernous sinuses. The sphenoidal sinuses are derived from a posterior ethmoidal cell that begins to invade the sphenoid, giving rise to multiple sphenoidal sinuses that open separately into the sphenoidal recess.
